note: Committed before the first RTH session of the competition period; the ledger holds only weekend abstentions at this point.

protocol.amendment_rule: any change is a new version with its own commitment, appended to data/protocol_commitments.jsonl and governing only the decisions recorded after it. Earlier versions are never deleted and keep governing the decisions taken under them.
protocol.hurdle_rule: total hurdle = round-trip fee (12.0bps, Bitget taker both sides) + deliberation cost, where deliberation = thinking_budget_ms priced against annualised volatility and the session depth multiplier (RTH 1x, extended 2x, overnight/weekend/holiday 3x). At LOW in RTH this is ~13.6bps and at the weekend ~18.8bps. The rule is fixed; the number moves with session and volatility and is recomputed every cycle by argus.agents.meta_pm.deliberation_cost_bps.
protocol.hypothesis: During US regular trading hours the desk will open positions, because the two-hour absolute move exceeds the total hurdle 58-86% of the time on eleven of twelve symbols (data/hurdle_clearance.json), and it will keep abstaining outside them. If the desk abstains through a full RTH week as well, the deliberation-cost hurdle is too high to trade this universe at all, and that is the finding we publish rather than a lowered bar.
known_weaknesses: The log began 2026-09-12, later than the two weeks the handbook recommends.
Bitget's demo environment carries no rTokens, so these fills are internal to ARGUS until an Agentic account routes the crypto hedge legs.
Sizing is a flat ceiling, not a volatility-scaled or Kelly-derived size; the Constitution may reduce it but nothing yet sets it from the evidence.
Three of the five official Bitget Skills carry no data from this network, so the evidence panel is thinner than the venue's tooling implies.
protocol.settlement_rule: every position is settled against a price fetched in a LATER cycle, never against a price available at decision time; abstentions are settled too, against the move that actually happened over the same horizon, so a correct refusal is gradeable

AMENDED FROM v1: the committed schedule read 'every 2 hours' plus the four RTH times. The 2-hourly trigger was removed on 2026-09-13 after every scheduled run from 08:52 died on a token budget sized for a smaller cycle and wrote nothing. It fired mostly into weekend and overnight sessions, which this protocol does not permit trading in, so no tradeable window was lost - but it WAS a committed schedule and removing it silently would have been the exact dishonesty this file exists to prevent. The four remaining triggers all sit inside the US regular session (13:30-20:00 UTC).

At this amendment the desk has made 126 decisions and every one was taken in a weekend or overnight session, which v1 already forbade trading in. The pre-registered hypothesis about regular hours is therefore UNTESTED, not refuted.

AMENDED FROM v2: v1 and v2 recorded exactly one observation per abstention, at ~24h. That is the one horizon at which a refusal cannot be scored, because consecutive 24h windows on 2h-spaced decisions overlap by ~92%. Decisions taken under v1/v2 keep their single observation and cannot be retro-marked — the prices are gone. So refusal accuracy is computable only from seq 232 onward, and anything earlier stays UNDEFINED rather than being back-filled from a price series fetched today.

A 1h horizon would be preferable and is NOT observable at this cadence: the committed cycle schedule is 2-hourly, so the earliest second look at any decision is ~2h. The marks therefore measure ~2h, which is also the horizon data/hurdle_clearance.json uses for the universe.
protocol.settlement_rule: every position is settled against a price fetched in a LATER cycle, never against a price available at decision time; abstentions are settled too, against the move that actually happened over the same horizon, so a correct refusal is gradeable AMENDED IN v3 (2026-09-15): in addition to the settlement above, every abstention is also marked once at a SHORT horizon in the first cycle at least 1.5h after the decision, and that mark is appended to data/refusal_marks.jsonl beside the ledger (never into it — the ledger is hash-chained and settles each entry exactly once). Reason, measured rather than asserted: across all 178 abstentions settled under v1/v2 the realised settlement horizon was minimum 24.02h, median 24.57h, maximum 36.39h, and decisions are taken 2h apart, so those 24h windows overlap by ~92% and the 178 rows carry on the order of three independent observations. Directional accuracy at that horizon is UNDEFINED and the marks exist to make it computable at a horizon that is not. Each mark records the horizon ACTUALLY measured, because a decision taken in the last cycle before the overnight gap is next seen ~18h later, not ~2h. No trading behaviour, hurdle, size or verdict changes under this amendment; it adds an observation only, and it can only make the desk's refusals easier to falsify.
